title: Strozzapreti with Tomato
subtitle: Hand-rolled pasta twists in a simple passata sauce
excerpt: Strozzapreti are short, rough-edged pasta twists from Emilia-Romagna. A garlicky passata sauce clings to the ridged surface. This is one of the quickest and most satisfying pasta suppers you can make.
sourceNotes: Emilia-Romagna tradition of strozzapreti with a simple tomato sauce, synthesised from standard Italian pasta cooking methods.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce keeps refrigerated for 3 days. Cook pasta fresh and reheat the sauce.

content.text: Strozzapreti have a rough surface that grips a smooth tomato sauce. Use a good passata for the cleanest flavour. Don't rush the garlic or it will turn bitter.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a low heat. Add the garlic slices. Cook gently for 2 minutes until pale gold. Do not let them brown.
Add the passata and chilli flakes. Season with salt. Simmer over a medium-low heat for 15 minutes until slightly thickened.
Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta according to the packet, then drain. Reserve a mugful of pasta water first.
Tip the drained pasta into the sauce. Toss over a low heat for 1 minute. Add pasta water to loosen if needed.
Remove from the heat. Stir through most of the basil. Serve with parmesan and the remaining basil leaves.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes sharp and acidic.
items.cause: The passata needs longer to sweeten and reduce.
items.fix: Simmer for 5 more minutes and add a pinch of sugar if needed.

items.cause: It browned or burnt before the passata was added.
items.fix: Start again with fresh garlic over a lower heat. Watch it closely.

items.symptom: The pasta absorbed all the sauce.
items.cause: Too much pasta or too little sauce.
items.fix: Add pasta water a tablespoon at a time and toss to coat.
